chief_complaint: recurrent painful draining boils in axillae and groin
hpi_details: 26-year-old obese female who smokes presents with recurrent, painful, deep-seated boils and draining sinus tracts in both axillae (armpits) and her groin for the past 2 years. They frequently rupture, leaving behind thick scars, and severely impact her quality of life.
ideas: She thinks the painful boils are severe ingrown hairs and sweat glands that keep getting infected from shaving and friction.
concerns: She is worried the foul drainage and thick scarring will push her partner away and force her to quit her retail job because moving hurts too much.
expectations: She hopes to get strong antibiotics and have the doctor lance the most painful lump today so she can get immediate relief.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Hidradenitis Suppurativa is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Hidradenitis Suppurativa: Oral Clindamycin + Rifampin, weight loss, warm compresses, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: recurrent painful draining boils in axillae and groin
Key HPI features: A 26-year-old obese woman who smokes has recurrent painful deep nodules, draining sinus tracts, and scarring in the axillae and groin for 2 years.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Hidradenitis Suppurativa.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Hidradenitis Suppurativa.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Recurrent furunculosis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Fever or rapidly spreading erythema/cellulitis — suggests systemic infection requiring escalation.
management_principles: Plan for Hidradenitis Suppurativa: Oral Clindamycin + Rifampin, weight loss, warm compresses
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 26F presenting with chronic, recurrent, painful, suppurative nodules and abscesses in intertriginous areas.
reference_soap.objective: Exam of the bilateral axillae reveals multiple deep-seated, tender inflammatory nodules, double-comedones (blackheads), draining sinus tracts, and hypertrophic 'rope-like' scarring. Groin shows similar but milder lesions.
reference_soap.plan: Advise weight loss and smoking cessation (major triggers). Prescribe topical clindamycin and a long course of oral antibiotics (e.g., Doxycycline or Minocycline). Consider referral to Dermatology for biologic therapy (Adalimumab) or surgical excision of sinus tracts.

teaching.one_liner: A chronic inflammatory follicular disease causing recurrent painful draining boils in the armpits and groin.
red_flags: Fever or rapidly spreading erythema/cellulitis — suggests systemic infection requiring escalation

must_ask.say: Where do the boils occur, and how often?
Does this run in your family?

history.answer: I keep getting these painful, swollen boils in both of my armpits and groin that constantly break open and drain pus.
It started about two years ago with small painful bumps under my arms, and over time they became deeper, spread to my groin, and formed tunnels under the skin.
They are mainly in my armpits on both sides and along the skin folds in my groin, nowhere else on my body.
They look like deep red swollen lumps that rupture and drain foul-smelling yellowish pus and blood, leaving thick rope-like scars.
They are very painful and throbbing, especially when they swell up or when my clothing rubs against them.
They sometimes itch or burn right before a new bump swells up, but the main issue is the throbbing soreness.
No, they do not disappear within hours; each lump persists for weeks or months, and new ones keep popping up.
I have had these flare-ups repeatedly for the past two years, and the short antibiotic courses I got at local clinics only gave brief temporary relief.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, fatigue, or generalized body aches.
No, I do not have any blisters, sores, or redness in my mouth, eyes, or inside my genital area.
No, my skin is not peeling off, and I do not have any dark purple spots or bruises.
No, I have never had swelling of my lips, tongue, or face, and I have no shortness of breath or dizziness.
No, I have not started any new prescription drugs, antibiotics, painkillers, or herbal medications recently.
No, I have not switched my laundry detergent, body wash, or deodorant, and I have not worn new jewelry or touched unusual plants.
My mother actually used to get similar recurrent boils in her armpits when she was younger.
No insect bites, no recent hiking or outdoor trips, and I have not visited public saunas, gyms, or pools.
I had mild eczema as a child, but I have no history of asthma or allergic rhinitis.
No, I do not have any joint pain, swelling, or changes in my fingernails or toenails.
I applied over-the-counter antibiotic ointments and tried warm compresses, but they did not stop the boils from coming back.
I have a single regular partner, we use condoms irregularly, and I have never had genital ulcers, blisters, or sexually transmitted infections.
I thought they were just really bad ingrown hairs and clogged sweat glands getting infected from shaving.
I'm terrified the smell and drainage will push my partner away, and the pain makes it almost impossible to stand and reach shelves at my retail job.
I'm hoping to get some strong prescription antibiotics and have someone lance this throbbing lump today so I can finally get relief.
I do not have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes, hypertension, or thyroid disease.
I have never had any surgeries, and I have never been hospitalized.
I am not taking any daily prescription medications, over-the-counter pills, or dietary supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I smoke about half a pack of cigarettes a day and have smoked for about six years.
I drink socially, about one or two beers once or twice a month.
I work as an office clerk sitting at a desk most of the day, and I live in an apartment with a roommate.
My father has hypertension, but there is no family history of psoriasis, lupus, or other autoimmune conditions.
My last menstrual period started two weeks ago, my cycles are regular every 28 days, and there is no possibility of pregnancy.

exam.finding: Alert, obese young female sitting comfortably on the examination table in no acute respiratory distress, moving arms cautiously due to axillary discomfort.
Blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, heart rate 74 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 36.8°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Conjunctivae are pink without pallor or discharge; sclerae are anicteric without injection.
Oral mucous membranes are moist and pink without mucosal erosions, aphthae, or ulcerations.
No cervical, submandibular, or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy palpable.

Bilateral axillae demonstrate multiple tender, deep-seated inflammatory nodules, open double-ended comedones, draining sinus tracts discharging purulent exudate, and thick rope-like hypertrophic bridging scars; no discrete breast masses palpable.

Bilateral axillae and inguinal folds show deep inflammatory nodules, sinus tracts, and rope-like scarring; surrounding skin elsewhere on the trunk and extremities is clear without generalized plaques, target lesions, or purpura.
Inguinal creases show tender erythematous subcutaneous nodules and mild comedones; labia and vaginal introitus are normal with no active mucosal ulcers or discharges.
No joint swelling, effusion, erythema, or tenderness across peripheral joints; nails show no pitting, oil drops, or onycholysis.
